html:
The Battle of Rivoli was fought on 14 and 15 January 1797 at Rivoli Veronese, between Lake Garda and the Adige River in northern Italy. The French army of the young general Napoleon Bonaparte beat a larger Austrian army under General Alvinczi.

In 1796 Napoleon had driven the Austrians out of Lombardy and shut one of their armies inside the fortress of Mantua. Austria tried four times to free it. In the last attempt Alvinczi came down from the Alps with about 28,000 men, split into several columns in the mountains. One French division held the plateau of Rivoli. Napoleon rushed there in the night with more troops, bringing his force to about 22,000. He beat the Austrian columns one by one as they arrived, then left to deal with a second Austrian force near Mantua. Alvinczi lost about 14,000 men, most of them prisoners.

Mantua surrendered on 2 February and Napoleon marched towards Vienna. Austria made peace in the Treaty of Campo Formio, which gave France control of northern Italy and ended the old Republic of Venice. The campaign, part of the French Revolutionary Wars, made Napoleon the most famous general in France.
